Felicia seats and sleeps 2 adults and is in great condition. She has been meticulously maintained with diesel synthetic oil changes every 10k miles and the turbo diesel runs strong and at a quiet purrrrrrr. The turbo was just replaced in August 2019 and supplementary components in June 2020. I did quite a bit of traveling with my partner and space/storage was never an issue.  Solar: - 2 x 100W Solar Panels on roof, charge 2 deep cycle batteries or whenever the van is running.  - 5 Outlets: 1 outlet available up front, 4 in the rear. Here is my original posting:   It is with great regret that I have now decided that I must abandon my “dream truck” project, which I paid a guy $20, 000 to get the truck to where it is.  He ripped me off and did not complete it, and now I've run out of time and money to do it myself.  My idea was that I wanted a restored truck with 1970’s technology rather than have all of the complicated electronic computer systems that they put in vehicles these days.  I figured that later on when I had the money I’d update the motor to a more modern one.  I decided to go with a 70s era Chevrolet because they are the most common truck from that decade, and therefore they still make parts for them.  I see 70s chevy trucks every day when I’m out driving around.  Plus there are 70s chevy trucks sitting in the fields of half the farms in America that perhaps people might be willing to part out.  For 40 years I’ve traveled all over the country in my work as a power plant and refinery construction welder, and I see them everywhere.  The truck I had for my camping and road trip truck was a 1973 Dodge D100.  I like the style of the Dodge more than the square body Chevy, and my Dodge had sentimental value for me because I did numerous camping trips and a couple road trips with my boys in it.  So I thought of putting the Dodge body onto a Chevy frame. I ran into a car restoration guy, L.D., in an auto parts store.  He said he could build the truck for me.  I hired him to do it, but he stopped working on it halfway through the project, and still kept it for a year and a half longer than we’d agreed on, etc.etc...  I won’t go into what I need to do to deal with that messy situation (court), but the main thing is I need to abandon my dream and sell this truck. So my ’73 Dodge Club cab body is mounted on a frame from a 1976 4x4 Suburban.  None of the wiring has been hooked up yet.  A laser light frame line up apparatus was used to cut and lengthen the frame to make room for the extended cab.  I’ve been a certified pipe welder for 40+ years and I did all the welding on the frame.  It came out super straight.  I used backup plates on the frame welds, and boxed in the frame at those locations.  Then I stitch welded a 2x3/8x36” inch cold rolled (hardened) skid bar on the bottom.
